title: Deterministic Client: Enforcing Determinism on Untrusted Machine Code
problem: Untrusted machine code exhibits non-deterministic behavior (timing variations, memory access patterns, scheduling dependencies) that complicates security verification and reproducibility. Enforcing determinism while maintaining performance is challenging without architectural support.
motivation: Deterministic execution of untrusted code enables reliable security analysis, debugging, and formal verification against timing-based attacks.
method: The system intercepts untrusted machine code and takes strict control of three normally-variable aspects: when instructions execute (timing), the order memory accesses happen, and how tasks are scheduled. By fixing these values, the code runs in the exact same way every time—making it deterministic. This control happens on your computer (client-side) rather than requiring special hardware, so performance is maintained.
key_novelty: The core idea is using controls on your computer to make untrusted code run in the exact same way every time, without needing special hardware or losing speed.
contributions: Deterministic Client system architecture for enforcing determinism on untrusted code
Mechanisms to eliminate non-determinism sources (scheduling, timing, memory ordering)
Performance optimization techniques to minimize determinism overhead
Evaluation on real untrusted programs demonstrating practical viability
primary_theme: Determinism enforcement for untrusted machine code
